issues.legal_issue: Civil contempt requires wilful disobedience of a court order that the person charged could comply with in normal circumstances.
material_facts: The approved revival scheme was not implemented fully, and the unit’s operation was affected by its old machinery, inadequate power supply, restrictions on removing machinery for repairs, and other difficulties.
The record indicated that the respondents were not directly responsible for all factors that prevented full implementation.
The Court found the material insufficient to establish that any respondent deliberately disobeyed the orders.
issues.conclusion: The charge of contempt was not established against any respondent, and the petition was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 129 of the Constitution and Section 2(b) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, civil contempt requires wilful disobedience of a court order or wilful breach of an undertaking. Wilfulness means voluntary and intentional conduct with a specific bad purpose to disobey or disregard the law. The order must be capable of execution by the person charged in normal circumstances, without extraordinary effort or dependence, wholly or partly, on an act or omission of a third party. The Court cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: contempt_proceeding and (implementation_depended_on_external_factors or compliance_required_extraordinary_effort) and (respondents_not_directly_responsible or evidence_does_not_establish_deliberate_disobedience)

predicates.contempt_proceeding: A party seeks a finding that a person wilfully disobeyed a court order.
predicates.implementation_depended_on_external_fact: Implementation was affected by events or circumstances beyond the charged persons’ direct control.
predicates.compliance_required_extraordinary_effort: Compliance could not be achieved in ordinary circumstances without extraordinary effort.
predicates.respondents_not_directly_responsible: The charged persons were not directly responsible for the circumstances preventing compliance.
predicates.evidence_does_not_establish_deliberate_d: The evidence did not establish that the charged persons intentionally disobeyed the order.

issues.definition: When a contempt proceeding concerns implementation affected by external factors or extraordinary effort, and the charged persons were not directly responsible or deliberate disobedience is not established, contempt is not established.

issues.legal_issue: Signing an implementation agreement with a different workers’ union does not amount to wilful disobedience when the petitioner union obstructs agreement and the alternative union is recognized by the authorities.
material_facts: The approved scheme envisaged an agreement involving the workers’ union, the State Government, and the new management.
Despite several meetings, the petitioner union’s president did not cooperate in reaching a tripartite agreement, according to reports from the Labour Commissioner.
The alternative union was the recognized union, and the State Government consented to an agreement with it.
The management entered into an agreement with the recognized union.
issues.conclusion: The agreement with the recognized union, rather than the petitioner union, did not amount to wilful disobedience of the Court’s orders.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(b) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 requires wilful disobedience. Conduct is wilful only when voluntary and intentional with a specific bad purpose to disobey or disregard the law. The Court cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: contempt_proceeding and petitioner_union_obstructed_agreement and alternative_union_was_recognized and authorities_approved_alternative_agreement

predicates.contempt_proceeding: A party seeks a finding that a person wilfully disobeyed a court order.
predicates.petitioner_union_obstructed_agreement: The union seeking to participate did not cooperate in reaching the required agreement.
predicates.alternative_union_was_recognized: The management made the agreement with a union recognized as representing the workers.
predicates.authorities_approved_alternative_agreeme: The relevant public authorities consented to the agreement with the alternative union.

issues.definition: If, in a contempt proceeding, the petitioner union obstructs agreement and the alternative union is recognized and approved by the authorities, entering the alternative agreement is not wilful disobedience.

issues.legal_issue: Incomplete payment and implementation of a court-approved rehabilitation scheme do not establish contempt when the record does not show wilful disobedience by the charged persons.
material_facts: The new promoter paid only two instalments of the agreed consideration but claimed to have made substantial investments in the unit.
The financial institution disbursed the Phase I term loan, and government departments took steps to obtain additional financing and working capital.
The unit faced operational difficulties, including problems with power supply and machinery, and implementation of the second phase had not commenced.
The Court considered the affidavits and found that the complete financial position could not be determined from the record.
issues.conclusion: The incomplete payments and scheme implementation did not establish contempt by any respondent on the material before the Court.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 2(b) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, civil contempt requires wilful disobedience, meaning voluntary and intentional conduct with a specific bad purpose to fail to do what the law requires. The Court held that failure to implement an order is not contempt unless the order was capable of execution by the charged person in normal circumstances and wilful disobedience is established. The Court cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: contempt_proceeding and scheme_implementation_incomplete and (substantial_performance_or_investment_occurred or implementation_faced_operational_obstacles) and financial_record_incomplete

predicates.contempt_proceeding: A party seeks a finding that a person wilfully disobeyed a court order.
predicates.scheme_implementation_incomplete: A court-approved scheme was not fully implemented or its required payments were not fully made.
predicates.substantial_performance_or_investment_oc: The charged persons or participating institutions made substantial payments, investments, or other implementation efforts.
predicates.implementation_faced_operational_obstacl: Operational or other practical difficulties impeded implementation of the scheme.
predicates.financial_record_incomplete: The available evidence did not provide a complete account of the financial position or implementation.

issues.definition: When a scheme remains incomplete but substantial implementation efforts or operational obstacles exist and the financial record is incomplete, the shortfall does not by itself establish contempt.
